content:
marta: heads up — hosted p95 jumped from 90ms -> 720ms across the us-west cluster around 16:03 UTC, p99 up to 1.6s. saw queue depth climb on the front-door. investigating. :eyes:

sam: yikes. any obvious deploys?

marta: no user-facing deploys in the window. infra shows a spike in requests to /v1/generate starting 16:02, but rate limits didn't trigger. looks like requests got stuck in our internal golden queue.

deploy-bot: deploy event: no active deploys in us-west at 2026-03-18T16:00:00Z

jing: can you paste the queue depth and routings?

marta: putting quick dump — filtered to the impacted router shard: 
```
router.shard=us-west-2-a
time,queued,processing,throughput
16:00:00,2,120,480req/s
16:02:00,18,128,475req/s
16:03:00,110,130,120req/s
16:04:00,90,80,98req/s
```

ryan: sudden queued=110 while processing didn't increase suggests backpressure somewhere downstream (workers not accepting). maybe kernel fallback on some hosts? perf-bot, any kernel-selection anomalies?

perf-bot: profiling summary (16:02-16:05):
- 12 hosts fell back from cuda-optimized kernel v3 -> scalar-emulate path after kernel-selector timed out (avg selection latency 1.2s)
- KV cache miss rate spiked from 7% -> 46% on those hosts
- batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 due to continuous preemption events
- observed sys_cpu steal on 6 hosts ~20% (noisy neighbor)

sam: that explains throughput drop. if kernel-selector timed out it forces slower path and increases latency -> upstream queueing. why did selector timeout?

marta: logs show selector RPC timeouts to kernel-info-service. the service was healthy but GC pause on 3 nodes correlated with the first timeout.

jing: GC on kernel-info-service? That svc should be tiny. ops-bot, any noisy tenant on the infra host pool?

ops-bot: alert: high I/O wait on gpu-node-43 (us-west-2-a) at 16:01:50, associated VMs: tenant-ff7, tenant-092. vm-mon reports heavy host-level backup job on tenant-ff7. :warning:

ryan: tenant backup = noisy neighbor. backup caused host IO and steal, kernel-selector RPCs latency increased -> timeouts -> many routers switched kernels to fallback -> batch collapse -> kv-cache churn because fallback path doesn't reuse KV layout -> miss storm.

marta: reproduction notes: I ran a small loadtest against the router with the selector intentionally delayed and saw p95 replicate. snippet: 
```
# simulate selector delay
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.us-west.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
done
```

sam: ok immediate mitigation options?

jing: 1) roll back selector hard timeout to be more conservative (increase timeout to 2s) 2) add circuit-breaker so hosts don't all fallback at once (stagger) 3) throttle tenant-ff7 backup or move it off GPU pool

marta: I pushed a canary to router to 20% with staggered fallback enabled (config flag: kernel.selector.stagger=true). observing now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy accepted: release/kernel-fallback-stagger -> 20% routers (us-west-2-a)

perf-bot: metrics after canary (16:10-16:20): p95 down to 140ms, p99 480ms; queue depth back to <10; KV miss rate falling to 12% on canary hosts.

sam: good. can we also add a temporary rule to rate-limit tenant-ff7 backup jobs at infra level? ops-bot?

ops-bot: creating infra rate-limit rule: `infra.blocking_io_limit` for tenant-ff7 scheduled immediate. notified infra team.

ryan: follow-up: we need longer-term fixes — selector rpc retry/backoff, fallback backoff (don't fallback if selector recovers quickly), cache warming when fallback occurs, and alerting for simultaneous kernel fallbacks per shard.

marta: creating ticket and will schedule postmortem. quick notes in ticket: 
- root cause: kernel-selector RPC latency due to host-level IO steal from noisy tenant running backup -> mass fallback to scalar path -> batch collapse and KV cache miss storm -> p95/p99 spike
- mitigations applied: staggered fallback canary + infra rate-limit on tenant-ff7
- action items: improve kernel-selector resilience, add staggering and circuit-breakers, KV cache warming strategy, alert on concurrent fallback events, ops policy for heavy IO jobs on GPU pool

jing: assigning tasks: @marta -> write postmortem skeleton, @ryan -> selector retries/backoff, @sam -> KV warming plan, @ops -> tenant policy enforcement

marta: thanks all. will update thread with postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
